params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

The small blue-purple star creature slaps a loose sketch flat onto the wall at its own head height, its whole body squashing on the hit. It spins on the spot, snatches another sheet off the floor, springs up and slaps that one onto the wall above the first. It drops down, grabs two more sheets at once, and slaps them up in a fast one-two, the row of sketches growing sideways across the wall. It bounces backwards and throws both arms wide at the wall it has filled.

Its face is exactly two round dark eyes and one small open smile, the same two eyes and the same smile in every frame. It has five points, the same five points in every frame. It lands on both feet on the floor after every leap. It stays small, no taller than half the height of the cabinet and the stacked boxes behind it, in every frame.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
